**Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on Surah 58, verses 3–4:**

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying:

﴿Those who divorce by zihar (a pre-Islamic form of divorce in which a husband declares his wife to be unlawful to him, as his mother's back) from among you, and then retract what they said, (the penalty is) the freeing of a neck before they touch one another. That is what you are admonished with, and Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ ﴿But whoever does not find (a slave), then (he must) fast two consecutive months before they touch one another. And whoever is not able, then (he must) feed sixty needy people. That is so that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger. These are the limits of Allah, and for the disbelievers there is a painful punishment.﴾

(p-246) People differed over the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿then they retract what they said﴾. Some said: the meaning is, "Those who used to make zihar in the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period)," as if He, Exalted is He, had said: "Those for whom zihar was a habit, then they return to it in Islam." This was said by al-Qutabi. The people of the apparent (Ahl al-Zahir) said: the meaning is, "Those who make zihar, then make zihar a second time." According to them, no expiation is required unless the man repeats the zihar. This was said by Mundhir ibn Sa'id. In that case, "returning" is a return to the statement which is reprehensible and false. This is a weak view, even though al-Qushayri related it from Bukayr ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Ashajj.

Some people said: in this verse there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir), and its implied form is: "freeing a neck for what they said." This too is a view that corrupts the structure of the verse. It is related from al-Akhfash, but it is not strong. Qatada, Tawus, Malik, al-Zuhri, and a great group of scholars said that the meaning of ﴿then they retract what they said﴾ is: by intercourse. That is, "then they retract what they said, namely that they would not return to it." So when a man makes zihar and then has intercourse, the expiation becomes obligatory upon him, and it remains binding on him even if he divorces or his wife dies.

Al-Shafi'i, Abu Hanifa, Malik as well, and a group of scholars said: "returning" means: with the determination to keep the wife and have intercourse with her, and the commitment to expiate for that. Thus, whenever this determination occurs from the one who made zihar, the expiation becomes binding upon him, whether he divorces or his wife dies. These two views are in the school of Malik, and both are good. The expiation is obligatory in both of them upon two conditions: zihar and return. It has been disputed what "return" is. Al-Shafi'i said: the return that makes the expiation obligatory is that he refrains from divorcing her after the zihar, and that, after the zihar, he lets pass the time in which he could have divorced her, and he does not divorce her.

The "neck" in zihar, according to Malik, is not acceptable unless it is a believing (mu'minah) slave. He returned this unqualified (mutlaq) term to the qualified (muqayyad) one found in the expiation for accidental killing.

People differed over His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿before they touch one another﴾. Al-Hasan, al-Thawri, and a group said: "before intercourse." They made "touching" (masis) here mean intercourse, and so they permitted the one who made zihar kissing, lying together, and enjoyment of the upper part of the woman's body, as in menstruation. The majority of scholars said: "before they touch one another" is general with respect to every kind of touching: intercourse and bodily contact. So it is not permissible for the one who made zihar to have intercourse, to kiss, to touch with his hand, or to do anything of this kind, except after the expiation. This is the view of Malik (p-247), may Allah have mercy on him.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That﴾ refers to "freeing (the neck)." That is, doing that is an admonition to you so that you may refrain from zihar.

Regarding "consecutive" (mutatabi') in the two months, it means fasting them, and one does not separate their days. It is permissible that a man fast them by counting, so he fasts sixty consecutive days. It is also permissible that he fast them by the lunar months: he begins with the crescent and breaks his fast with the crescent. If one of his two months is short (of thirty days), that suffices for him. It is also permissible, if he begins his fast in the middle of a month, to begin with part of the first month, fasting until the crescent, then fast a month by the crescent, then complete the first month by counting. I do not know of any disagreement among scholars that the one who fasts for zihar, if he breaks the consecutiveness by his own choice, must begin the fast anew. They differed if he breaks it due to a compelling excuse, such as illness, forgetfulness, and the like. Abu Hanifa's companions (Ashab al-Ra'y), al-Shafi'i in one of his two views, al-Nakha'i, Ibn Jubayr, al-Hakam ibn 'Uyayna, and al-Thawri said: he begins anew. Malik, al-Shafi'i in another view, and others said: he builds upon what he has done. They all agreed concerning a menstruating woman that she builds upon the consecutiveness in her fasting.

Feeding the needy in zihar is with the Hashimi mudd according to Malik, and it is a mudd and a third by the mudd of the Prophet (ﷺ). It was also said: two mudds, not a third. Ibn Wahb related from him that one feeds two mudds by the mudd of the Prophet (ﷺ). Among the scholars is one who holds that feeding in zihar is one mudd by the mudd of the Prophet (ﷺ). In feeding for zihar, it is not sufficient except to complete the number of the needy, and it is not permissible to feed thirty people twice or anything resembling that. The food is the staple food (ghalib qut) of the land. Malik, 'Ata', and others said: feeding the needy is also before touching, analogous to manumission and fasting. Abu Hanifa and the majority of scholars said: Allah, Exalted is He, did not stipulate the condition here, so we bind ourselves to it. Therefore it is permissible for the one who made zihar, if he is able to feed, to have intercourse and enjoyment before the expiation.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That so that you may believe﴾ refers to the concession and ease in moving from freeing a slave to fasting and feeding. Then He stressed it with His saying: ﴿And these are the limits of Allah﴾, that is: so commit to them and stop at them. Then He threatened the disbelievers with this statement and this legal ruling.

There is no private conversation among three but that He is their fourth, nor among five but that He is their sixth, nor less than that nor more but that He is with them wherever they are. Then He will inform them of what they did on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾

These verses were revealed concerning the hypocrites and a group of the Jews who were in Medina, who used to wrangle with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), await misfortunes to befall him, plot against him, wish harm for him, and hold secret consultations about that. Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 58, verses 9–10:

﴿O you who believe, when you hold private consultation, do not consult together in sin, transgression, and disobedience to the Messenger; but consult together in righteousness and piety. And upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾

In this verse, Allah Most High enjoins the believers not to hold private consultations about what is disliked, and this applies generally to all people until the Day of Resurrection. Allah, blessed and exalted is He, specified "sin" (al-ithm) by mention because of its comprehensiveness, and "transgression" (al-'udwan) because of its gravity in itself, since it consists of wrongs done to people. Likewise, "disobedience to the Messenger" was mentioned as a rebuke of the hypocrites, since their private consultations were about that.

The majority of readers recited "fa-la tatanajaw" (لا تَتَناجَوْا) on the pattern of "tatafa'alu". Ibn Muhaysin recited "fa-tanajaw" (فَتَناجَوُا) with one of the two tā's omitted. Some reciters recited "fa-la tannajaw" (فَلا تَّناجُوا) with a doubled tā', because the tā' was assimilated into the tā'. Al-A'mash and the people of Kufa recited "fa-la tantijaw" (فَلا تَنْتِجُوا) on the pattern of "tafta'ilu". The people read the ʿayn of "al-'udwan" with a ḍamma, but Abu Haywa read it with a kasra wherever it occurs. Al-Dahhak and others recited "wa-ma'siyyatu al-Rusul" (وَمَعْصِيّاتُ الرُسُلِ) in the plural in both places.

Then He commanded private consultation in righteousness and piety, and reminded them of the gathering (al-hashr), in which is the reckoning and entry into one of the two abodes.

As for His saying, "innama al-najwa" (إنَّما النَجْوى), "innama" here is not restrictive (lil-hasr), but is for emphasis of the statement. The scholars differed concerning the private consultation that is from Satan, which He informed of in this verse. A group of the exegetes said: the meaning is, "private consultation in sin, transgression, and disobedience to the Messenger is from Satan." Qatada and others said: the reference is to the private consultations of the hypocrites and the Jews. 'Abdullah ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: the reference is to the private consultation of a group of Muslims who intended to confer privately with the Messenger (ﷺ) while having no need or necessity for it, and they only wanted to appear to be doing so. The Muslims would think that such private consultation concerned news of an approaching enemy or something similar. These two views are supported by what follows in the wording of the verse, while the first view is not supported by it. 'Ata al-'Awfi said concerning this verse: it was revealed concerning the private conversation that a believer sees in a dream that distresses him, and what the sleeper sees is like a private conversation in which he is engaged. This view is foreign to the meaning that precedes it and the meaning that follows it.

Nafi' and the people of Medina recited "li-yuhzina" (لِيُحْزِنَ) with a ḍamma on the yā' and a kasra on the zāy, so the verb is attributed to Satan. Abu 'Amr, al-Hasan, 'Asim, and others recited "li-yahzuna" (لِيَحْزُنَ) with a fatḥa on the yā' and a ḍamma on the zāy. You say "ḥazantu qalb al-rajul" (حَزَنْتُ قَلْبَ الرَجُلِ) when you cause sorrow in him, so it is like your saying "kaḥalati al-ʿayn" (كَحَلَتِ العَيْنُ), and it is a kind of transitivity in which the object is like an adverbial of place. Sibawayh, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned this meaning among the transitive verbs. Some people recited "li-yaḥzana" (لِيَحْزَنَ) with a fatḥa on the yā' and the zāy, and in this reading "alladhina" (الَّذِينَ) is in the nominative, since the verb is attributed to them. It is said: "ḥazina al-rajul" (حَزِنَ الرَجُلُ) with a kasra on the zāy.

Then Allah Most High informed that Satan, and the private consultation that comes from him, does not harm anyone, except that it becomes a harm by Allah's permission, that is, by His command and decree. Then He commanded the believers to rely upon Him, blessed and exalted is He. All of this strengthens the view that the private consultation that is from Satan is precisely that which causes fear to the believers. Concerning the anxiety that afflicts hearts in this matter, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: « "Two should not confer privately to the exclusion of a third." »

**Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 58, verses 11–12:**

The words of the Exalted and Majestic:

﴿O you who believe, when you are told, "Make room in the assemblies," then make room; Allah will make room for you. And when you are told, "Rise up," then rise up; Allah will raise those of you who believe and those who have been given knowledge by degrees. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ ﴿O you who believe, when you consult the Messenger privately, offer a charity before your private consultation. That is better for you and purer. But if you do not find [the means], then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

(p-252) Most of the people recited "تُفْسِحُوا" (tufsihū). Al-Hasan and Dawud ibn Abi Hind recited "تَفاسَحُوا" (tafāsahū). Most of the qurra' (reciters) recited "فِي المَجْلِسِ" (fi al-majlis, in the singular "assembly"). ʿĀṣim alone, along with Qatada and ʿIsa, recited "فِي المَجالِسِ" (fi al-majālis, in the plural "assemblies").

The scholars differed concerning the occasion of revelation of the verse and what it intends. Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan and Mujahid said: it was revealed concerning the seats of war and fighting. Zayd ibn Aslam and Qatada said: it was revealed because of the people's crowding in the gathering of the Prophet (ﷺ), for they used to compete for closeness to him, for hearing his speech and for looking at him. A man who had the right, the seniority and the precedence in Islam would come and find no place, so this verse was revealed on account of that. Muqatil said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a group of people get up so that elders from among the people of Badr could sit, and the verse was revealed. Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No one should make another man rise from his seat and then sit in it himself; rather, make room, and Allah will make room for you."

Some people said: the verse is specific to the gathering of the Prophet (ﷺ), and it applies to all other gatherings as well. What indicates this is the reading of the one who recited "فِي المَجْلِسِ." And whoever recited "فِي المَجالِسِ" also intends this, because everyone has a place in the house of the Prophet (ﷺ) and its location, so it is collected under this meaning. The majority of the people of knowledge said: the cause is the gathering of the Prophet (ﷺ), but the ruling is general and applies to all gatherings that are for acts of obedience. From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The most beloved of you to Allah are those who are most gentle in their shoulders in prayer and in their knees in gatherings." This is the view of Malik (may Allah have mercy on him), who said: "I see the ruling as applying to gatherings of knowledge and the like, for all time." What supports this view is the reading of the one who recited "فِي المَجالِسِ." As for the one who recited "فِي المَجْلِسِ," it is, according to this interpretation, a noun of genus. Thus the recommended practice (sunnah) is making room, and standing up (for the sake of taking another's seat) is forbidden. The hadith of the Prophet (ﷺ) is that he "forbade that a man rise from his place so that another sits in it." As for standing out of reverence, it is permitted by the hadith, namely his (ﷺ) saying when Saʿd ibn Muʿadh (may Allah be pleased with him) came: "Stand up for your master" (p-253). It is obligatory upon the one who is honoured not to like this and not to make people do it, for the saying of the Prophet (upon him be blessings and peace): "Whoever loves that men stand before him, let him take his seat in the Fire."

As for the saying of the Exalted, ﴿Allah will make room for you﴾, its meaning is: in His mercy and His Paradise.

As for the saying of the Exalted, ﴿And when you are told, "Rise up," then rise up﴾, its meaning is: when you are told, "Rise and stand," then do so. From this comes "nushūz al-ʿiẓām," meaning the growth of bones. And "al-nashz" from the earth is the elevated ground. The words of the Mighty and Majestic:

﴿Are you apprehensive that you should offer charity before your private consultation? They are neither of you nor of them, and they swear by a lie while they know.﴾ ﴿Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. Indeed, evil is what they have been doing.﴾ ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield, and so they averted [people] from the way of Allah; for them is a humiliating punishment.﴾

"Al-Ishfaq" (apprehension): fear of being unable to give the thing that is given in charity, or fear of the loss of wealth through charity. It has many meanings in which the word ishfaq is used, but in this place it is as I have mentioned. ﴿And Allah turned to you﴾ means: He returned to you (with mercy).

As for His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿So establish prayer﴾, the verse, its meaning is: persist in these deeds which are the foundations of your law. As for the one who said that this charity was abrogated by the verse of zakat, his saying is weak; the conditions of abrogation (naskh) are not met. What is reported in this regard from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, is not authentically from him. And Allah the Exalted knows best.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Have you not considered those who have taken as allies﴾. It was revealed concerning a group of the hypocrites who took as allies a people from the Jews, who are "those upon whom is anger." Al-Tabari said: "They" refers to the hypocrites, "of you" refers to the believers, and "of them" refers to the Jews.

The Qadi Abu Muhammad, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

This interpretation accords with the Exalted's words: ﴿wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those﴾ [al-Nisa: 143], and with the words of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: "The example of the hypocrite is the example of a goat wandering between two flocks," because he is with the believers by his speech and with the disbelievers in his heart. According to this interpretation, the action of the hypocrites is more fitting, because they took as allies a people upon whom is anger, who are not of themselves, so their protection does not bind them, nor of the righteous people, so that alliance would be correct. However, this verse admits of another interpretation, namely that the Exalted's words "They are not of you" refer to the Jews, and His words "nor of them" refer to the hypocrites. According to this interpretation, the action of the hypocrites is more fitting, because they took as allies a people upon whom is anger, who are not of themselves, so their protection does not bind them, nor of the righteous people, so that alliance would be correct. And His words "and they swear" mean the hypocrites, because whenever they became aware of what they were doing of hatred toward the Prophet, peace be upon him, and insulting him, and allying with his enemy, they swore that they would not do that, and considered breaking the oath a trivial matter. Many incidents of this kind have been reported, which I have abridged for brevity; if they were traced in the books they would be found, such as the saying of Ibn Ubayy: "If we return to Medina..." and his oath that he had not said it, and other things.

"The severe punishment" is the punishment of the Hereafter. The majority of readers recited "aymanahum" (their oaths), plural of yamin; al-Hasan recited "iymanahum" (their faith), i.e., what they display of faith.

"Al-Junnah": that by which one is concealed and protected from what is feared; from it comes "al-mijann," which is the shield. The Exalted's words ﴿so they averted [people] from the way of Allah﴾ may be understood as an intransitive verb, as you say: "Zayd turned away," i.e., they themselves turned away from the way of Allah and faith in His Messenger. It may also be understood as transitive, i.e., they turned other people away from faith, from those who followed them and walked in their path. It may also mean: they averted the Muslims from killing them, and that is the way of Allah concerning them; but by what they displayed of faith they averted the Muslims from that. "Al-Muhin": the humiliating one, from humiliation (al-hawan).

Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 58, verse 17–21:

His the Mighty and Majestic's saying:

﴿Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them anything against God. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.﴾ ﴿On the Day when God resurrects them all, and they swear to Him as they swear to you, and they think that they are upon something. Verily, it is they who are the liars.﴾ ﴿Satan has overpowered them and caused them to forget the remembrance of God. Those are the party of Satan. Verily, the party of Satan are the losers.﴾ ﴿Indeed, those who oppose God and His Messenger, those are among the most humiliated.﴾ ﴿God has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail." Indeed God is Strong, Mighty.﴾

It is narrated that the hypocrites took pride in the abundance of their wealth and children and displayed their joy at that, so the verse was revealed informing that this brings them no benefit from God and no defense through it. The governing element (al-'amil) of His, exalted is He, saying "Yawm" (on the Day) is "ashab" (companions), by way of an implied verb (taqdir fi'l).

God, exalted is He, informs in this verse about them that there will be oaths for them on the Day of Resurrection, and before God, they will imagine through their ignorance that these oaths will benefit them and be accepted from them. This is their reckoning, that they are "upon something", i.e., upon an action, i.e., something beneficial for them. Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said, in the Book of al-Tha'labi: (p-257) The prayer and peace of God be upon him said: "A caller will call on the Day of Resurrection: Where are the adversaries of God? Then the Qadariyya will come with faces blackened and eyes blue, and they will say: 'We did not worship the sun, nor the moon, nor an idol, nor did we take any god besides You.'" Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: "They spoke truthfully, by God, but shirk came upon them from where they did not know." Then he recited this verse.

His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿Satan has overpowered them﴾ means: he took possession of them from every direction and prevailed over their souls. This verb is used according to its original form ('ala al-asl), for the analogy of morphological derivation (qiyas al-ta'lil) would require that it be said "istahaza" (with the alif), and al-Farra' mentions in the Book of "al-Lughat" that 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, recited "istahaza".

"Yuhaddun" means: they assign to themselves a limit (hadd) of actions and sayings. Some scholars of meanings said: its meaning is: they are in a limit other than the limit God, blessed and exalted, has legislated. Then God, exalted is He, decreed humiliation upon its opponent, and informed that He decreed, in what He enacted of His judgment and decree from eternity, that He and His messengers will overcome everyone who opposes God and the messengers. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read "wa-rusulī" with a fathah on the yā', and the rest read it with sukun. Al-Hasan said: God never commanded a messenger to fight except that He made him prevail and gave him victory by His strength and might; there is no lord besides Him. Others said: whoever is not commanded to fight is victorious by proof (bil-hujjah).

Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 58, verse 22:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified:

﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers or their sons or their brothers or their kinsmen. Those - He has written within their hearts faith and supported them with a spirit from Him. And He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. Those are the party of Allah. Unquestionably, the party of Allah - they are the successful.﴾

This verse negates that there could be found one who believes in Allah, exalted is He, with the true faith and who adheres fully to its branches, loving a disbeliever or a hypocrite. The meaning of "yuwaddu" (loving, showing affection) is that between them there is such gentleness that each of them loves the other. On this interpretation, some of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, said: "O Allah, do not make for a polytheist any favour upon me that would be a cause of affection, for You say:" and he recited this verse. The verse may also intend: there is no one who believes in Allah and the Resurrection who loves one who opposes Allah insofar as he is opposing Him, for then he would love opposition, and that necessitates that he would not be a believer.

It is narrated that this verse was revealed concerning the matter of Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a and his writing to the people of Makkah. (p-258) The apparent meaning of these verses is that they are connected in meaning, and that this is in the sense of censure of the hypocrites who allied themselves with the Jews. If we say it was about the matter of Hatib, then that comes as something separate regarding the matter of the hypocrites, though it resembles it. The "ikhwan" (brothers) here means brothers by lineage, as evidenced by its being paired with "fathers." "Ikhwan" is known to be used for friends of affection, just as "ikhwa" is known for kinship by blood, and it may be used in the sense of brotherhood of love. "Kataba fi qulubihim al-iman" means: He established it and created it by bringing it into existence. Abu 'Ali al-Farisi and others among the Mu'tazilah held that the meaning is: He placed in their hearts signs by which the angels know that they are believers, because they see the servant creating his own faith. Al-Naqqash expressly stated this doctrine, and I do not think he said it except without having grasped what he said; as for Abu 'Ali al-Farisi, he spoke with insight into it.

The majority of readers recited "kataba" with the verb in the active form, and "al-iman" in the accusative. Abu Haywa and 'Asim, in the transmission of al-Mufaddal from him, recited "kutiba" with the verb in the passive form, and "al-iman" in the nominative.

His saying, may He be exalted: "Ula'ika" (those) is a reference to the believers whom the meaning of the verse requires, because the meaning is: "Rather, you find them not loving those who oppose Allah." His saying, may He be exalted: "bi-ruhin minhu" (with a spirit from Him) means with guidance, gentleness, light and divine success that springs forth from the Qur'an and from the words of the Prophet (ﷺ). It was also said the meaning is: with the Qur'an, because it is a spirit. It was said the meaning is: with Gabriel, peace be upon him.

"Al-hizb" (the party) is the group united by a single creed, and "al-muflih" (the successful) is the one who attains his desired aim. The rest of the verse is clear.

The tafsir of Surah [al-Mujadila] is complete, and praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
